evidence.title: Guinea-Bissau holds referendum on expanding presidential powers ahead of election

occurrences.checkable_against: Guinea-Bissau referendum records and election calendar
occurrences.quote_span: Guinea-Bissau is voting Sunday in a referendum to decide on granting new presidential powers ahead of December’s general election, which will return the West African nation to democracy after its latest coup.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: Public statements by Guinean political analysts and constitutional process records
occurrences.quote_span: Analysts say the military government lacks the legitimacy to change the constitution, which has sparked discontent among the citizens.
occurrences.speaker: Analysts
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: AP interview transcript or recording with Gen. Tomás Djassi
occurrences.quote_span: “In a community, there is only one leader. No community or village can have two leaders. We revised the constitution to avoid constant conflict between the president of the republic and the prime minister. We clarified the law and helped the public understand that the president of the republic is the national symbol. It is the president who stands for election in presidential polls,” Gen. Tomás Djassi, the head of the armed forces, said.
occurrences.speaker: Gen. Tomás Djassi
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: Public statements by Guinea-Bissau opposition groups
occurrences.quote_span: Opposition groups reject the claim.
occurrences.speaker: Guinea-Bissau opposition groups
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: Text of Guinea-Bissau proposed constitution and referendum result
occurrences.quote_span: If passed, the new constitution by the self-styled National Transitional Council will grant more powers to the president and reduce parliamentary representation, among other issues.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: Statement by Guinean political analyst Paulino Quadé
occurrences.quote_span: “The fundamental question is: Who drafted this Constitution, and on whose behalf? To protect which interests or institutions? Who stands to benefit from this Constitution?” Paulino Quadé, a Guinean political analyst, said.
occurrences.speaker: Paulino Quadé
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: AP interview transcript with Carolina Djeme
occurrences.quote_span: “I’ll go vote on Sunday. However, I’ll vote ‘no’ because — honestly, and I think this is the case for many other citizens — I don’t know this new Constitution well, so I can’t vote ‘yes’,” she said.
occurrences.speaker: Carolina Djeme
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: UN Office on Drugs and Crime trafficking reports on Guinea-Bissau
occurrences.quote_span: The country is a hub for drug trafficking between Latin America and Europe, an issue experts say fuels its political instability.
occurrences.speaker: Experts and outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: World Bank country and poverty data for Guinea-Bissau
occurrences.quote_span: The tiny country of around 2.2 million people has the highest proportion of natural wealth per capita, according to the World Bank, but more than half of the country lives in poverty.
occurrences.speaker: World Bank and outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: AP interview transcript with Carolina Djeme
occurrences.quote_span: Another resident in Bissau, Carolina Djeme, said the constitution is unfamiliar to her.
occurrences.speaker: Carolina Djeme
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: Guinea-Bissau historical records of independence and coups
occurrences.quote_span: Since it gained independence from Portugal in 1973, the only Portuguese-speaking West African country has been rocked by several coups and attempted coups.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: Proposed constitution text and Guinea-Bissau parliamentary records
occurrences.quote_span: The authorities argue that a parliament trimmed from 102 to 65 seats would allow for easier and more robust debates, while new presidential powers would underline the higher authority of the president over the prime minister, which they claim is a source of political instability in the country.
occurrences.speaker: Guinea-Bissau transitional authorities
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: AP interview transcript with Muniro Conté and proposed constitution text
occurrences.quote_span: “This constitution significantly weakens the Prime Minister and the government, subordinates the National People’s Assembly and political parties
occurrences.speaker: Muniro Conté
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: AP interview transcript with Bacar Camará
occurrences.quote_span: “The transitional government should focus on creating conditions for better understanding and reconciliation among Guineans,” he said.
occurrences.speaker: Bacar Camará
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: AP interview transcript with Bacar Camará
occurrences.quote_span: Bacar Camará, a high school teacher in the capital, Bissau, said he would not be voting and disapproves of the referendum, citing a fraught political and social environment.
occurrences.speaker: Bacar Camará
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: Public statements and boycott directives issued by Guinea-Bissau opposition groups
occurrences.quote_span: But the opposition has called on voters to boycott the referendum, saying it is a path for the head of the military government to amass power and calling it a “source of political instability at all levels”.
occurrences.speaker: Guinea-Bissau opposition
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers

occurrences.checkable_against: Guinea-Bissau voter registry and polling or survey data on the constitution
occurrences.quote_span: Nearly 915,000 voters are registered to vote in the referendum, but the majority say the constitution is not a problem.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Guinea-Bissau referendum approval of a new constitution expanding presidential powers
